deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is an archival folder cover (Umschlag) from the Göttingen Gauss Nachlass, written by a later archivist, not by Gauss. It records:
(1) The shelfmark: 'Math 1 A 6' struck through and replaced by the current signature 'Math. 2'.
(2) The subject heading 'Arithmetik und Algebra'.
(3) The sub-heading 'A. Zu den Disquisitiones arithmeticae gehörig' (material belonging to the Disquisitiones Arithmeticae).
(4) Item 6, 'Tafel der Formen der quadratischen Reste ...' (table of the forms of quadratic residues), with a pencilled reference number '1081'. That number may be a catalogue or inventory number, or a page reference; its exact meaning is uncertain.
(5) 'Enthält: Gauß 40 f/1-10': the folder contains leaves 1-10 of an older numbering 'Gauß 40 f'.
(6) A rubber stamp 'nach alter Sign.' (according to the old signature), followed by a stamped symbol.

The content described is probably a table connected with Disquisitiones Arithmeticae §§ 97-152 and the appended Tabula I/II. Those tables give quadratic residues and the linear forms of divisors of x^2 - A, i.e. the classes of primes for which a given number is a quadratic residue. Tables of this kind appear in Werke Bd. II. Nothing can be reconstructed or checked from this cover itself.

results.what: Archival description: a table of the (linear) forms of quadratic residues, i.e. forms of primes for which a given number is a residue, belonging to the Disquisitiones Arithmeticae material
results.modern_name: Table of quadratic residue characters / linear forms of prime divisors of x^2 - a (quadratic reciprocity tables)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), Tabula I-II; earlier Euler and Lagrange for such forms

deep.surprise_reason: This is a folder cover with catalogue information only. It contains no mathematical content, and the described table belongs to well-known Disquisitiones material.
transcription_corrections: The heading word is 'Arithmetik und Algebra' (archivist's hand). The transcription is correct here.
'Math 1 A 6' is struck through, and '2' (the new signature Math. 2) is written below in pencil.
'6.' is item number 6 under section A, consistent with the old signature 1 A 6. It could be misread as 'b.' but '6' fits the old shelfmark.
The pencilled '1081.' after 'Reste ...' is a later addition in a different hand. It is likely a catalogue or inventory reference.
'Enthält: Gauß 40 f/1-10' and the stamp 'nach alter Sign.' are archival notes, not Gauss's hand.
